messages:
maya: Quick summary from a short calibration run for the low-touch profiler we talked about yesterday. Did a mix of sampled nsys runs and a few full traces on a p4d-equivalent node.
liam: nice — was this on dedicated infra or a canary pool?
santiago: curious about numbers (overhead / variance) — please paste commands and a tiny excerpt of output.
maya: This was on a dedicated test pool (3x A100 80GB). Workflow: 1) baseline p99 with no tracing and synthetic workload, 2) nsys sampled runs (1% sampling) across 2k requests, 3) 10 full short traces for worst-case delta.
maya: Command we used (nsys sampling):
```
nsys profile --output=tmp_prof --trace=cuda,cudnn,osrt --sample=cpu --cpucycles --force-overwrite --sampling-period=1000 
# we kept sampling period coarse to reduce overhead, and excluded memcpy events in postproc
```
olivia: why sample=cpu instead of mixed?
maya: sampling on cpu lowers the frequency of GPU-side instrumentation; pairing with --trace=cuda gives kernel timelines but reduces driver/probe overhead. We also post-filter kernel names to focus on attention/softmax/gemm.
liam: numbers?
maya: Short excerpts:
- baseline p99 (no tracing): 73ms
- sampled 1% p99: 75ms (+2.7%)
- sampled 5% p99: 84ms (+15%)
- full trace p99: 110ms (+50%)
We also measured token throughput: sampled 1% ~ -3% throughput, 5% ~ -12%, full trace ~ -40%.
santiago: interesting — big nonlinearity beyond ~2-3%. which kernels got blown up in full traces?
maya: Full traces show heavy serialization on kernel launches and memcpy synchronization. Main offenders: small-k GEMMs (per-head matmul with seq len <64), softmax kernel launches (many tiny kernels). Sampling preserves kernel timeline shape but misses some short-lived microbatches.
rachel: any evidence profiler changed KV cache behavior? i.e., probe caused extra misses or different eviction?
maya: Good catch — we saw a small increase in cold-loads when running full traces: ~1.8% more kv-miss signals in the first 10 requests of a session. Hypothesis: the tracer serializes some memcpy/io causing slight timing shifts that prevent the in-flight KV prefetch from hitting. Sampled runs did not show measurable delta within noise.
santiago: So safe plan is: sampled tracing as default, full traces only on-demand with canary gating. Do we have a calibration algo to pick sampling rate per model/region?
maya: Prototype heuristic:
- Compute per-kernel duration mean and stddev from a small population of full traces (10-20) offline.
- Define acceptable measurement error e.g., target margin-of-error on mean kernel latency = 5% at 95% CI.
- Translate that into required sample count n via z * sigma / (E * mu) => n = (1.96 * sigma / (E * mu))^2.
- Cap n to a max fraction of QPS (default 1%). For short/high-variance models this allows up to 3-5% temporarily.
- Add a backoff: if live p99 delta > 8% compared to baseline running sample, reduce sampling by half and notify.
liam: Can you explain the sigma / mu part in plain terms?
maya: Sure — sigma is kernel latency stddev, mu is mean latency. The ratio sigma/mu is coefficient of variation. Higher CV -> need more samples to get stable mean. For example a microkernel with CV=0.6 needs many more samples than a big GEMM with CV=0.05.
olivia: How do we avoid profiler perturbing short-kernel scheduling (the thing that made full traces bad)?
maya: A few tactics: 1) avoid tracing memcpy/back-to-back context switches (filter these events), 2) use coarse CPU sampling (bigger sample period), 3) defer sampling probe attachment until KV warmup window completes (e.g., start sampling after first 4 tokens), 4) for seq < 128 prefer sample-only not full.
santiago: What about KV cache probes specifically? If probe touches the same memory paths we might evict or serialize.
maya: We implemented a light kv-probe that only records hit/miss counters via in-process counters (ATOMICS) instead of async io tracing. That reduced observable perturbation to below noise at 1% sampling. Full tracing path, which inspects buffers, caused the 1.8% cold-load blip.
rachel: Are we going to expose a per-model sampling config in the console?
maya: Plan: yes. Console defaults derived from offline calibration per-model-version. Settings: sample_rate (0.1%-5%), warmup_tokens, kernel_whitelist (regex), hard_cap (max fraction), and safety_fallbacks (p99-delta threshold).
liam: Any performance regression safety hooks? e.g., auto-disable tracing on CI/alerts?
maya: We added two guardrails:
- Local auto-throttle: if sampling-induced p99 increase > 8% for two consecutive 5-minute windows, drop sampling by 50% and create an alert.
- Global safety cap: never allow sampling to exceed 10% on production routes without manual approval.
olivia: Ops questions: who gets alerted?
maya: Alert -> eng-runtime on-call + model-owner alias. Infra-bot posts a short automated summary with sampled rate, delta, and last-full-trace-id.
infra-bot: Deploy note — sampling config updated for model-id=redwood-opus-v1 in prod-canary: sample_rate=1%, warmup_tokens=4.
santiago: One more thought — should we use adaptive sampling by seq length? e.g., higher rate for long sequences because they expose tail kernels?
maya: Agreed. Our prototype increases sample rate linearly with seq_len beyond 1024 up to 5%. Rationale: longer sequences have more kernel launches and more chance of rare slow paths (e.g., KV fallback).
liam: Any artifacts I can run locally to reproduce the calibration?
maya: Pushed a tiny script to repo infra/profiler/calibrate.sh — it runs 500 synthetic requests, collects kernel histograms, then computes suggested sample_rate. Example run command pasted in thread:
```
./calibrate.sh --model ./models/test-quant --node-type p4d --target-e=0.05 --max-frac=0.03
```
maya: Action items:
- olivia: please hook the calibrator output into the console defaults (PR next week).
- santiago: add a small unit test that verifies backoff triggers when p99 delta > 8%.
- liam: try the calibrator on the memory-optimized pool and report numbers.
- rachel: update the runbook with the guardrail thresholds and who to page.
maya: I'll also schedule a small canary run with adaptive seq_len sampling and post results here. :rocket:
liam: thanks — this is actionable.
maya: any objections to the 1% default?
santiago: fine by me, seems conservative.
olivia: fine.
rachel: +1.
maya: closing for now, will post raw CSVs and the small perfetto timeline extract after the canary run.
